headline.caveat: two-year prototype OTA ceiling (Jul 2025) — subsequently effectively destroyed by the Feb 2026 government-wide ban; Anthropic is litigating

realized_to_date.caveat: obligated amounts never publicly itemized; whatever was obligated is now in a six-month phase-out

nature_md: July 14, 2025: DoD's CDAO awarded Anthropic a two-year prototype OTA with a $200M ceiling to 'prototype frontier AI capabilities that advance U.S. national security' — part of the same four-lab award wave as OpenAI/Google/xAI. Under a separate July 2025 arrangement, Claude became the first frontier model approved for classified networks, with the Pentagon agreeing to Anthropic's acceptable-use policy (no mass domestic surveillance of Americans, no fully autonomous target selection/engagement). The relationship then inverted: the Pentagon demanded 'all lawful purposes' usage without AUP limits, negotiations failed, and on **Feb 27, 2026** the President directed all federal agencies to cease using Anthropic's technology while Defense Secretary Hegseth designated Anthropic a **'supply chain risk'** — barring any DoD contractor, supplier, or partner from commercial activity with Anthropic, with a six-month phase-out. GSA removed Anthropic from USAi.gov and its multiple-award schedules. Anthropic sued the Defense Department over the designation on Mar 9, 2026. The edge is now a negative: the $200M ceiling stands as a monument to a federal pipeline that was killed over usage-policy principles.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Obligations against the ceiling were never publicly itemized; the ban halts new obligations and forces contract wind-down. The supply-chain-risk designation extends the effect beyond direct contracts to Anthropic's entire defense-contractor customer base.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Whatever federal revenue existed is being phased out; the larger P&L hit is indirect — defense contractors (a major enterprise segment) are barred from using Anthropic products for military work, and GSA delisting cuts civilian-agency channels. Anthropic's commercial (non-government) growth continued regardless; litigation outcome could restore or permanently bar the channel.

both_sides_md: **Government framing (attributed):** the Pentagon cannot depend on a critical supplier that reserves the right to refuse lawful military uses — dependency without assurance is a supply-chain risk (Hegseth directive). **Anthropic framing (attributed):** the AUP terms were agreed contractually in July 2025 and the designation is retaliation for refusing to drop safety commitments — it sued rather than concede (Mar 2026 suit); reporting noted Claude had been used in the June Iran operation even as the designation landed (CNBC).

events.title: CDAO awards Anthropic two-year, $200M-ceiling prototype OTA; Claude first frontier model on classified networks
Federal agencies ordered off Anthropic products; DoD designates it a 'supply chain risk'
events.why_it_matters: Kills Anthropic's federal pipeline government-wide (GSA delisting, contractor bar, six-month phase-out) — the first destruction of a lab-government relationship over acceptable-use terms, and a template for political counterparty risk that no revenue model prices.

events.title: Anthropic sues the Defense Department over the supply-chain-risk designation
